title: CVE-2021-22876: Automatic referer leaks credentials
explain: The evidence does not settle it either way.
receipts_override: judge quoted an external source that does not say that (https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/rfc/inline-errata/rfc9421.html)
summary: The --referer ';auto' feature copies the current URL verbatim into the Referer header of subsequent requests, potentially leaking credentials in logs.

claims.text: The current URL is copied as-is to the referrer header of the subsequent request when using --referer ';auto'
claims.reasoning: The provided patch shows the vulnerable code in Curl_follow does a direct strdup of data->change.url without stripping credentials or fragment.

citations.note: Patch shows original code: data->change.referer = strdup(data->change.url); copies URL as-is including credentials and fragment

claims.text: in lib/transfer.c in the Curl_follow function
claims.reasoning: The patch diff header and context confirm the location is lib/transfer.c in the Curl_follow function.

citations.note: Patch context shows the code is in Curl_follow function in lib/transfer.c

claims.text: using --referer ';auto' with a URL containing credentials or fragment
claims.reasoning: The http_auto_referer flag is set when ';auto' is used, and the vulnerable code executes when this flag is true with a URL containing credentials or fragment.

citations.note: Patch shows condition: if(data->set.http_auto_referer) which is set by --referer ';auto'

claims.text: credentials may appear in third party web server logs
claims.reasoning: The Referer header is sent to the next server in a redirect chain. When the URL contains user:pass credentials, they are included in the Referer header and can appear in third-party server logs. External source E1 confirms this is a recognized security concern.

citations.note: Referer header gets the full URL with credentials via strdup(data->change.url)
External source confirms: 'The Referer header should not expose credentials or URL fragments'

claims.text: run curl -svLe ';auto' 'https://user:pass@curl.haxx.se#frag' and grep for Referer
claims.reasoning: The reproduction command uses --referer ';auto' with a URL containing credentials and fragment, which triggers the vulnerable code path.

citations.note: Reproduction would show Referer header containing 'user:pass' and '#frag' from the original URL

key_reasons: The patch demonstrates the flaw: Curl_follow copies the full URL (including user:pass and fragment) to the Referer header via strdup(data->change.url) when http_auto_referer is set.
The fix correctly uses the URL API to parse the URL and explicitly clear CURLUPART_USER, CURLUPART_PASSWORD, and CURLUPART_FRAGMENT before using the URL as Referer.
This is a privacy-sensitive information leak: credentials in URLs (though discouraged) are exposed to redirect targets via the Referer header.
The deterministic checks confirm the code at revision bd6b54ba1f55 (master on submission date) contains this flaw.
External source E1 confirms the security best practice that Referer headers should not expose credentials or fragments.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and patch. The issue is confirmed: Curl_follow in lib/transfer.c copies the full URL including credentials and fragment to the Referer header when --referer ';auto' is used. Your fix correctly uses the URL API to strip user, password, and fragment parts. This is a valid privacy-sensitive information leak. We will apply the fix.
